customer_joe: Hey — a subset of users can't finish OAuth sign-in (Google + GitHub). They hit an error in our client: "Authorization failed: invalid_grant (state mismatch)". Happens ~1-2% of attempts, intermittent. Repro steps I used: log in with Chrome Mobile, choose Google, approve, redirect back to our /auth/callback, then we get the error.

alice_support: Thanks Joe — can you paste the full callback URL (redacted client_secret) and any server logs around the moment? Also which region + CDN?

customer_joe: Sure. Using us-east, CloudFront in front of our proxy. Sample failed callback URL (redacted):

https://app.example.com/auth/callback?code=4/0AY0e-gXXX&state=eyJhbGciOiJI..&session=abc123

Server log snippet at time of failure:

```
ERROR oauth.handler: state verification failed, expected=eyJhbGciOiJI..., got=eyJhbGc... (truncated)
WARN oauth.handler: PKCE verifier not found in session
INFO proxy.forward: forwarded with query string set to 1
```

bob_oncall: Two quick suspects: 1) proxy/CDN is rewriting or truncating query params, 2) double-state param or encoding mismatch (plus vs %20 or base64url differences). Can you check the raw request headers we see at the app (x-forwarded-for + raw querystring)?

customer_joe: Raw request line we receive from proxy: 

GET /auth/callback?code=4/0AY0e-gXXX&state=eyJhbGciOiJI..&state=dup_ie HTTP/1.1
Host: app.example.com
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 11)

alice_support: Oh, there's a duplicate state param (`state=...&state=dup_ie`). Some reverse proxies/analytics middlewares append tracking params and accidentally add state again. OAuth libraries typically pick the first or last param depending on parser — leads to mismatch.

carla_cs: Customer-facing workaround: ask affected customers to clear any tracking cookies or disable the analytics Chrome extension if present. Not great though.

bob_oncall: Root cause: our proxy had a tiny plugin that appends `state` for an internal flow when it sees `?`. It runs for certain user agents (mobile UA) to track redirect origins. That explains the ~1-2% mobile skew.

alice_support: Recommended fixes:
- Remove/disable the plugin that appends query params (hotfix).
- Normalize incoming query params in app: if multiple `state` keys, prefer the last one OR validate both PKCE_verifier/session exists.
- Register exact redirect_uris (avoid wildcard or trailing slash mismatches).

bob_oncall: Quick safe hotfix deployed to proxy: rolled back the analytics plugin at 11:24 UTC. dev_ops_bot: deploy v2.3.1 completed :white_check_mark:

dev_ops_bot: [deploy] service/proxy v2.3.1 rolled out to edge nodes (us-east) — rollback available.

customer_joe: After rollback, tested with same repro on Chrome Mobile — login succeeded twice in a row. Thanks!

alice_support: Follow-ups for product backlog:
- Add check that rejects OAuth callback if PKCE_verifier missing with a more helpful error (log GUID + return user-friendly message).
- Add monitoring alert for duplicate query params on /auth/callback (count > 0.1%).

carla_cs: I'll message impacted accounts with the root cause and ETA for full fix.

bob_oncall: Long-term: avoid relying on proxies to mutate auth URLs; if analytics requires attribution, use postRedirect attribution (fragment) or server-side session association.

customer_joe: Huge help, thanks all :raised_hands:

alice_support: Marking this thread resolved for now. Reopen if you see more failures.
